What comes up in Hurstville

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table is what the work usually involves here rather than a statement about any particular property.

Commercial frontage with neighbours either side

Attached structures where the party walls have to be left standing and weatherproof.

How it is handled
Walls propped and supported, the roof junction detailed, then hand demolition at the boundaries and machine work only where it is safe.
What does it
Smaller machines working off the footprint, hand tools at the junctions.

Multi dwelling site ahead of a basement

The redevelopment pattern here: something comes down and a basement goes in.

How it is handled
A planned structural demolition behind hoarding, then the dig to the retention design with the spoil classified before it moves.
What does it
Large excavator with a grapple, then a toothed bucket, bogie tippers where the street is tight.

Attached and shared structures

Semis, terraces, duplexes and shopfronts joined to something that stays standing. The job is as much about what is retained as what is removed.

How it is handled
Propping and support to the retained side, hand demolition at the junction, then the wall made weatherproof and left in a condition the neighbour can live with.
What does it
Hand tools and small plant at the junction, with a machine used only where it is safe to do so.

Hurstville

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Strong apartment redevelopment Around the centre, which brings unit block demolition and basement excavation rather than knockdowns.
  • Attached commercial frontages Where the job is defined by what has to stay standing and weatherproof.
  • Dense surroundings Neighbouring buildings close and footpaths in use, so hoarding and traffic management are part of the job rather than extras.
  • Older residential stock behind the centre With the usual pre 1990 asbestos assumptions.

Around central Hurstville there is rarely a laydown area, so spoil and rubble leave as they are generated and the trucks are sequenced against the machine. Where a truck and dog cannot stand or turn, the same volume goes out in considerably more tipper loads.

Hurstville questions

What people ask before we start

Can you work while the shops next door stay open?
Yes, and it is common here. It means hoarding, dust and noise control, agreed hours and a sequence that keeps the neighbouring access open. It is slower than an empty site and it is quoted that way.
Is the basement dig part of the same job?
It can be, and on a redevelopment site it usually should be. One contractor means the shoring, the batter and the truck movements are planned once rather than handed over midway.
How does a basement dig follow a demolition here?
Better as one contract than two. One contractor means the shoring, the batter and the truck movements are planned once, which matters on the tighter sites near the station precincts.
How many contractors am I dealing with if there is asbestos on site?
One. Max holds demolition licence AD214737, licensed asbestos removalists carry out the removal, and an independent licensed assessor does the air monitoring and clearance. Sequencing the three of them is our job, not yours.
